answer: Dynamic Identity Sinking imposes a rising resource tax on parallel nodes. When an agent requests network bandwidth to reach a consensus summit, it must emit continuous proof-of-work anchored to a unique hardware chip. Cloning an agent forces both instances to share a single internal ferrous core register, splitting their processing clock cycles in half. Because the network measures computational throughput per channel, duplicating an identity drops efficiency below the profitability threshold of a lonely karst cave miner.
